question: Does repeated PEFT LoRA merge/unmerge used by TRL weight synchronization mutate the original BF16 base weights, and does out-of-place/safe merge prevent it?
primary_hypothesis: For a nonzero LoRA delta, PEFT 0.19.1 unsafe merge followed by unmerge can produce bitwise changes in BF16 base weights because both operations round in the storage dtype. A zero-delta arm should remain exact. Float32 is a precision control, not a claim that all deployments use it.
scope: Numerical integrity of one source-level synchronization path only. This is not a model-capability experiment and does not establish prevalence or downstream training impact.

source_provenance.trl_path_observed: merge_adapter() before vLLM parameter transfer; unmerge_adapter() after transfer

protocol.target: first transformer block q_proj only; LoRA rank 4, alpha 8, dropout 0
protocol.adapter: synthetic deterministic nonzero adapter initialized from a seeded Gaussian, with B overwritten to nonzero values; no learned adapter is available, so results are numerical-path evidence only
arms: BF16 functional baseline: do not merge; verify base parameter bytes unchanged after 100 synchronization-equivalent no-op iterations
protocol.primary_metric: number of changed base-weight elements after each roundtrip; exact byte equality to pre-merge tensor
secondary_metrics: fixed-prompt logits max absolute difference before/after roundtrips
protocol.decision_rule: Reproduction passes if the nonzero BF16 unsafe arm has at least one changed base-weight element after 10 cycles and both zero-B and functional controls are bitwise exact. An exact/no-drift result rejects this reproduction under the chosen adapter and layer. Safe merge is descriptive; do not assume it is safe against roundtrip drift until measured.
protocol.resource_ceiling: Cached q_proj tensor only (896x896); CPU only; process RSS <=2 GiB and elapsed <=5 minutes; no network/model download.
protocol.stopping_rule: one locked run; no tuning adapter scale, target layer, seed, or thresholds after observing outcome
protocol.claim_boundary: A pass demonstrates a reproducible numerical defect in this pinned path/configuration only. It does not establish material effect on policy quality, frequency in trained adapters, or current maintainers' deployment configurations.
protocol.measurement_fixture: Extract model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight directly from the pinned cached safetensors shard; wrap a one-layer nn.Module exposing q_proj with PEFT 0.19.1. This isolates the exact library arithmetic while avoiding a full-model load.
